full.description: This image shows a gross pathology specimen of a human liver slice. The liver parenchyma appears diffusely yellowish-brown and shows a finely granular, smooth texture. This appearance is characteristic of diffuse metabolic or storage diseases, such as alpha-1 antitrypsin deficiency or early cirrhosis, where fat accumulation and architectural alterations give the liver a pale yellow color.

random.description: This is a gross specimen photograph showing a cross-section of a liver. The organ appears enlarged and exhibits a smooth, yellowish-tan discoloration distributed diffusely throughout the parenchyma. These macroscopic features are characteristic of hepatic steatosis, commonly known as a fatty liver.
